about.title: Gridley Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Gridley is a town of about 6,582 people, the kind of place where a death touches more than one household. When that loss happens because someone else was careless — a driver on Route 99 or Magnolia Street, a property owner who ignored a hazard, a company that cut corners — California law gives certain family members a way to hold that party accountable in civil court. Public records show 11 injury collisions in Gridley in 2025, with 11 people hurt and no traffic deaths that year; the highest collision counts fell along Route 99, Magnolia Street, Spruce Street and Sycamore Street, with reports peaking on Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Wrongful death claims here also arise from farm and workplace incidents, medical care, and defective products. A wrongful death case is separate from any criminal proceeding. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Butte County families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so asking questions doesn't add a bill to what you're already carrying.

whyChoose.title: Why Gridley Families Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases — a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can tell you quickly whether you or another relative should be the one to file.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched for you
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Getting connected early keeps those deadlines from slipping by while your family is grieving.

items.title: The full picture of what can be recovered
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Your attorney will walk through each category with you, at no cost unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My parent died in Gridley and I'm one of several adult children. Can we all be part of the claim?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children are first in line to bring a wrongful death action. Siblings generally join together in one case rather than filing separately, and an attorney can explain how that works and who else, such as certain dependents or heirs, may have a right to participate. The consultation arranged through LawProactive is free.

items.question: The crash happened on Route 99 near Gridley. Does it matter that it's a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If part of the claim involves a public agency — for example, a question about roadway maintenance or a government vehicle — California requires a claim to be presented to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is one reason families in Butte County are encouraged to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later, even if the facts are still coming together.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution in Butte County. Evidence from the criminal case can sometimes be helpful, but your family's two-year filing deadline does not pause while the criminal matter plays out. An attorney can help you decide how the two proceedings should fit together.
